artworks.title: Theseus Slaying the Minotaur (tondo of the Aison Kylix)
artworks.description: The Aison kylix tondo: Athens' hero pins the Minotaur in the labyrinth — the deed that crowns the Theseus cycle.

artworks.title: Theseus Victorious over the Minotaur
artworks.description: A Pompeian wall-painting freezes the aftermath: Theseus stands over the slain bull-man, the labyrinth's tribute ended.

artworks.title: The Minotaur
artworks.description: Watts' brooding Minotaur — the creature at the heart of the cycle, waiting in Knossos for the tribute ship.

artworks.title: Theseus Slaying the Minotaur
artworks.description: Barye's bronze compresses the labyrinth combat into a single violent knot of hero and bull.

artworks.title: Ariadne Abandoned by Theseus
artworks.description: Kauffmann's abandoned Ariadne — the cycle's bitter coda after the Minotaur falls and the black sails set for Athens.

popCulture.title: Minotaur
popCulture.description: Theseus' Attic cycle still orbits the labyrinth — the tribute ship, Ariadne's thread, and the bull-man under Knossos.

popCulture.title: Theseus
popCulture.description: Athens' culture-hero remains the unifying king of the cycle — robber-slayer, labyrinth victor, and founder of the synoikismos.
